39: `serialize`. There is no execution/issuance/queue dispatch method. An entry is an
40: immutable OBSERVATION identity, not a mutable job. States describe submitted data;
41: new observation ids never authorize or execute work. This deliberately does not
42: implement a job state machine or classify execution-qualified incidents. Nisi
43: integrity and receipt contracts remain unchanged, opaque payload data here; no
44: receipt reader, canonical profile or issued-plan WeakSet is copied or replaced.
45: 
46: ### Closed input and time rules
47: 
48: Config has exactly `{projectId,maxEntries,heartbeatTtlMs,redactPaths}`. IDs (all
49: id fields and stage) match `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,127}$/`. `maxEntries`
50: is a positive safe integer <=10000, `heartbeatTtlMs` a positive safe integer.
51: `redactPaths` is an array of distinct dot paths starting `payload.` with at least
52: one subsequent segment, each segment ASCII identifier `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`
53: or canonical nonnegative array index `0|[1-9][0-9]*`. No `__proto__`, `prototype`,
54: or `constructor` segments, duplicate paths or ancestor/descendant overlap.
55: Retain their input order. Invalid config throws Error with `.code === 'CONFIG'`.
56: 
57: Every entry has exactly these keys, all mandatory:
58: 
59: ```text
60: id, projectId, runId, attempt, candidateId, stage, receiptId,
61: createdAt, ttlMs, state, heartbeatAt, retryOf, revokes, payload
62: ```
63: 
64: `attempt` is a nonnegative safe integer. `receiptId`, `retryOf`, `revokes` are
65: nullable IDs. `state` is one of QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED/REVOKED.
66: `createdAt` is a nonnegative safe integer in caller-defined milliseconds, `ttlMs`
67: positive safe integer, and their sum must also be safe. `heartbeatAt` is null
68: or nonnegative safe integer <=createdAt. It can be supplied on any state;
69: only RUNNING uses it for liveness. REVOKED requires non-null `revokes` and null
70: `retryOf`; every other state requires null `revokes`. Non-null retryOf requires
71: QUEUED (a syntactically valid other state returns REFUSED RETRY below).
72: 
73: Inputs are ordinary trusted data objects, not hostile Proxies. Clone without
74: executing accessors: reject accessors, symbols, non-enumerable fields, extra array
75: properties/holes, cycles, non-plain objects, undefined/functions/bigints, non-safe
76: integer numbers, malformed Unicode strings, negative zero, and dangerous object
77: keys `__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor` anywhere. JSON payload may otherwise
78: be any JSON value. Plain Object.prototype or null-prototype records and dense
79: arrays are supported. Invalid entry or createdAt > append now throws code ENTRY.
80: 
81: `append(entry, now)`, `list(now)` and `retain(now)` require a nonnegative safe
82: integer `now` >= the journal watermark (starts 0). Invalid/backwards now throws
83: code TIME, without mutation. The watermark advances only on a successful append,
84: list or retain. DUPLICATE, CONFLICT, REFUSED and thrown calls do not advance time
85: or change stored records. `serialize()` reads no time. No clock/random/fs/network.
86: 
87: ### Identity, observations and relationships
88: 
89: Append first checks time, snapshots/validates the entry and createdAt<=now. A
90: sealed journal then returns REFUSED SEALED. A projectId different from the config
91: returns REFUSED PROJECT. Compute original fingerprint H(`nisi-run-journal/input/v1`
92: + newline + C(entire original entry)), before redaction. If id already exists,
93: matching fingerprint returns exactly `{status:'DUPLICATE',id}`; differing returns
94: `{status:'CONFLICT',id,reason:'ID_CONTENT_MISMATCH'}`. Check seen identity BEFORE
95: redaction path resolution, relationships or retention. Never replace, renew,
96: un-revoke or resurrect an existing entry, including historical/tombstone entries.
97: 
98: For an unseen id with retryOf: require QUEUED, earlier target in this journal,
99: same runId, strictly greater attempt, createdAt>=target.createdAt, and target
100: terminal (SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED/REVOKED), expired at supplied now, or revoked
101: by a prior entry. Candidate may change on retry. Otherwise REFUSED RETRY.
102: Stale/missing heartbeat alone is never sufficient. For an unseen revocation:
103: target must already exist, match runId/attempt/candidateId and have
104: target.createdAt<=entry.createdAt; otherwise REFUSED REVOCATION. Revoke effects
105: are monotonic; another revocation may cite an already revoked target, including
106: a revoking entry, but cannot undo its old effect. All relationship fields stay
107: in identity metadata when payloads are pruned. There is no deletion operation.
108: 
109: Every refusal is exactly `{status:'REFUSED',id,reason}`. Otherwise redact/capture,
110: insert in arrival order, advance watermark, enforce retention, then return
111: exactly `{status:'APPENDED',id}`. Earlier entries are never modified except for
112: payload retention. Successful appends can record already-expired observations;
113: these lose their payload immediately and confer no authority.
114: 
115: ### Redaction and retention
116: 
117: For NEW input, every configured redaction path must resolve via own data fields
118: in that entry; otherwise throw code REDACTION, without mutation. Replace its
119: entire value (scalar/object/array) by literal `[REDACTED]`. Arrays use canonical
120: index segments only, and traversal through a primitive is invalid. Capture only
121: the REDACTED entry plus its original fingerprint; do not retain raw secret
122: payloads or canonical original strings in the journal closure. Caller objects
123: are not mutated. Thus getter snapshots AND serialized records are redacted.
124: Config is fixed for the lifetime and serialized with the journal; it is not part
125: of entry identity and cannot be edited via API. Fingerprints are equality aids,
126: not secret protection against guessing or authentication. This isolated sorted
127: JSON digest profile is NOT the Nisi canonical/integrity/receipt profile.
128: 
129: Retention prunes only payloads: mark `retained:false`, set `entry.payload:null`,
130: keep ALL identity/attribution/state/time/links/fingerprint metadata forever.
131: First prune each retained entry whose `now >= createdAt+ttlMs`; then prune oldest
132: remaining retained entries by insertion order until retained count<=maxEntries.
133: Never delete ids; total identity metadata is explicitly unbounded in this v1.
134: `retain(now)` applies that rule, advances watermark, returns frozen newly-pruned
135: ids in original insertion order. `list(now)` does the same retention/time work,
136: then returns a frozen ordered array of exactly these per-entry views:
137: 
138: ```text
139: {entry, historical, retained, revoked, expired, liveness, authorizing:false}
140: ```
141: 
142: `historical` is false for this instance's fresh appends, true for EVERY reopened
143: entry, permanently, including DUPLICATE replay. `revoked` means any accepted
144: entry cites this id via revokes; a REVOKED state's own target does not revoke
145: itself. `expired` is now>=createdAt+ttlMs even on terminal entries. `liveness`
146: precedence: revoked -> REVOKED; terminal state -> original state; expired ->
147: EXPIRED; RUNNING with null heartbeat or now-heartbeatAt>heartbeatTtlMs -> UNKNOWN;
148: otherwise original state. Equality at heartbeat window is still RUNNING.
149: No liveness classification grants issuance, retry, or execution authority.
150: 
151: ### Canonical serialization and prefix reconciliation
152: 
153: C(value) is compact JSON with recursively sorted object keys (JS default lexical
154: sort), original array order and JSON escaping; no whitespace, trailing spaces or
155: raw embedded line breaks. H(text) is lowercase SHA-256 of UTF-8 text. The only
156: allowed import is `{createHash}` from `node:crypto`, used for deterministic H.
157: No other export/import or side effects are needed. Checksums detect accidental
158: damage and ordering errors, not malicious rewriting with recomputed hashes.
159: 
160: `serialize()` emits canonical newline-delimited JSON, with final newline required
161: after EVERY line. Exactly one header, all entry records, one footer. Shapes:
162: 
163: ```text
164: header = {type:'header',schema:'nisi-run-journal-v1',config,now:watermark}
165: record = {entry:redactedOrPrunedEntry,fingerprint:originalFingerprint,retained:boolean}
166: envelope = {type:'entry',seq,previousHash,record,hash}
167: footer = {type:'footer',count:entryCount,lastHash}
168: ```
169: 
170: Initial previousHash=H(`nisi-run-journal/header/v1` + newline + C(header)).
171: Sequence starts at 1. Envelope hash=H(`nisi-run-journal/record/v1` + newline +
172: C({seq,previousHash,record})), and becomes next previousHash. Footer lastHash
173: is final envelope hash (header hash if empty). Store neither historical nor
174: authority flags in serialized records. Complete reopen then serialize without
175: mutation MUST return identical bytes. Capture ownership, not serialized input,
176: sets historical=true. An input payload claiming issued/PASS is still data.
177: 
178: `reopen(serialized)` takes a string (other types treated as invalid header) and
179: never throws on malformed serialized data. It returns `{journal,report}`. Report
180: has exactly `{status,recoveredIds,rejectedLine,reason,authorizing:false}` with
181: status COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE/INVALID. recoveredIds is the exact valid prefix in
182: order. No guessed lost count. rejectedLine is 1-based physical line or null.
183: 
184: Require canonical bytes and exact keys on all parsed objects. JSON duplicate
185: keys, extra fields, unknown version/status or pretty printing fail the canonical
186: roundtrip check. Header invalid, missing or not newline-terminated: INVALID,
187: reason HEADER, rejectedLine 1, recoveredIds [], journal null. A valid header
188: creates a journal with that config/watermark. Validate each NEWLINE-TERMINATED
189: record before recovering it: exact schema, entry schema and same project, entry
190: createdAt<=header.now, fingerprint and hashes lowercase 64-hex, next seq/chain,
191: unique id, valid earlier retry/revocation target, retained boolean, null payload
192: if !retained. Retained payload must have all redaction paths already equal to
193: the marker; pruned payload skips path checks. Retained expired entries and count
194: beyond maxEntries are invalid. On reopen, fingerprint is opaque original-input
195: equality metadata: do not recompute it from redacted/pruned payload. Link validity
196: is checked against prefix using header.now; target metadata and revocation links
197: are available even after payload pruning. Never recover an offending record.
198: 
199: Stop at first bad record: INVALID/RECORD at its line, ignore all later lines.
200: A line that does not parse as canonical JSON is RECORD; its intended type is
201: unknown. FOOTER applies only to a recognized canonical object with type footer.
202: Missing footer after last complete newline: INCOMPLETE/MISSING_FOOTER at next
203: line. A non-newline-terminated tail after header: INCOMPLETE/TRUNCATED at that
204: line; even a parseable JSON record without newline is NOT recovered. Footer
205: shape/count/lastHash mismatch: INVALID/FOOTER at that line. Any bytes after a
206: valid footer (even another newline or incomplete tail): INVALID/TRAILING_DATA
207: at the immediately next physical line. Valid footer and end: COMPLETE, null
208: reason/rejectedLine. All recovered records are historical, including on damage.
209: 
210: If report is not COMPLETE but header was valid, return the recovered journal
211: SEALED. It permits list/retain (time still validated) but every syntactically
212: valid append, even an identical replay, returns REFUSED SEALED. serialize throws
213: code SEALED. No API clears this seal: absence of a missing id cannot be proven.
214: Sealing errors and reports never claim file persistence, original authenticity,
215: reconciled external effects or fresh issued execution evidence.
